arxiv-1511-07004.title: Understanding Music Playlists
arxiv-1511-07004.creator: Keunwoo Choi, György Fazekas, Mark Sandler
arxiv-1511-07004.description: Abstract As music streaming services dominate the music industry, the playlist is becoming an increasingly crucial element of music consumption. Consequently, the music recommendation problem is often casted as a playlist generation problem. Better understanding of the playlists is therefore necessary for developing better playlist generation algorithms.

arxiv-2112-07381.title: You Only Need One Model for Open-domain Question Answering
arxiv-2112-07381.creator: Haejun Lee, Akhil Kedia, Jongwon Lee*, Ashwin Paranjape, Christopher D. Manning, Kyoung-Gu Woo * ♣ \clubsuit Samsung Research ♢ \diamondsuit Samsung Electronics ♠ \spadesuit Stanford University ♡ \heartsuit Growdle Corporation {haejun82.lee, akhil.kedia, jay722.lee}@samsung.com{ashwinp, manning}@cs.
arxiv-2112-07381.description: Abstract Recent approaches to Open-domain Question Answering refer to an external knowledge base using a retriever model, optionally rerank passages with a separate reranker model and generate an answer using another reader model. Despite performing related tasks, the models have separate parameters and are weakly-coupled during training.

arxiv-2205-09069.title: Influence of Magnetic Fields on the Gas Rotation in the Galaxy N ​ G ​ C ​ 6946 NGC\;6946
arxiv-2205-09069.creator: M. Khademi, S. Nasiri, F. S. Tabatabaei
arxiv-2205-09069.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by M. Khademi, S. Nasiri, F. S. Tabatabaei. Magnetic fields can play an important role in the energy balance and formation of gas structures in galaxies. However, their dynamical effect on the rotation curve of galaxies is immensely unexplored. We investigate the dynamical effect of the known magnetic arms of N ​ G ​ C ​ 6946 NGC\;6946 on its circular gas rotation traced in HI, considering two dark matter mass density models, ISO, and the universal NFW profile.

arxiv-2210-05027.title: Probabilities of Causation: Adequate Size of Experimental and Observational Samples
arxiv-2210-05027.creator: Ang Li, Ruirui Mao, Judea Pearl
arxiv-2210-05027.description: Abstract The probabilities of causation are commonly used to solve decision-making problems. Tian and Pearl derived sharp bounds for the probability of necessity and sufficiency (PNS), the probability of sufficiency (PS), and the probability of necessity (PN) using experimental and observational data.

arxiv-2304-08299.title: Accurate and Definite Mutational Effect Prediction with Lightweight Equivariant Graph Neural Networks
arxiv-2304-08299.creator: Bingxin Zhou, Outongyi Lv, Kai Yi, Xinye Xiong, Pan Tan, Liang Hong, Yu Guang Wang
arxiv-2304-08299.description: Abstract Directed evolution as a widely-used engineering strategy faces obstacles in finding desired mutants from the massive size of candidate modifications. While deep learning methods learn protein contexts to establish feasible searching space, many existing models are computationally demanding and fail to predict how specific mutational tests will affect a protein’s sequence or function.

arxiv-2507-21884.title: Exploration on Demand: From Algorithmic Control to User Empowerment
arxiv-2507-21884.creator: Edoardo Bianchi
arxiv-2507-21884.description: Abstract Recommender systems often struggle with over-specialization, which severely limits users’ exposure to diverse content and creates filter bubbles that reduce serendipitous discovery. To address this fundamental limitation, this paper introduces an adaptive clustering framework with user-controlled exploration that effectively balances personalization and diversity in movie recommendations.

arxiv-2512-09611.title: Real-Time Non-Smooth MPC for Switching Systems: Application to a Three-Tank Process
arxiv-2512-09611.creator: Hendrik Alsmeier, Felix Häusser, Andreas Knödler, Armin Nurkanović, Anton Pozharskiy, Moritz Diehl, Rolf Findeisen
arxiv-2512-09611.description: Abstract Real-time model predictive control of non-smooth switching systems remains challenging due to discontinuities and the presence of discrete modes, which complicate numerical integration and optimization. This paper presents a real-time feasible non-smooth model predictive control scheme for a physical three-tank process, implemented without mixed-integer formulations.

arxiv-2602-05466.title: Optimization is Not Enough: Why Problem Formulation Deserves Equal Attention
arxiv-2602-05466.creator: Iván Olarte Rodríguez, Gokhan Serhat, Mariusz Bujny, Fabian Duddeck, Thomas Bäck, Elena Raponi
arxiv-2602-05466.description: Abstract Black-box optimization is increasingly used in engineering design problems where simulation-based evaluations are costly and gradients are unavailable. In this context, the optimization community has largely analyzed algorithm performance in context-free setups, while not enough attention has been devoted to how problem formulation and domain knowledge may affect the optimization outcomes.

arxiv-2602-10518.title: MapVerse : A Benchmark for Geospatial Question Answering on Diverse Real-World Maps
arxiv-2602-10518.creator: Sharat Bhat, Harshita Khandelwal, Tushar Kataria, Vivek Gupta
arxiv-2602-10518.description: Abstract Maps are powerful carriers of structured and contextual knowledge, encompassing geography, demographics, infrastructure, and environmental patterns. Reasoning over such knowledge requires models to integrate spatial relationships, visual cues, real-world context, and domain-specific expertise-capabilities that current large language models (LLMs) and vision–language models (VLMs) still struggle to exhibit consistently.

pmc-11438207.creator: Vivian P. Mushi, Winifrida Kidima, Isolide S. Massawe, Pendo F. Magili, Dan Bhwana, Rahel Elishilia Kaaya, Henrika Kimambo, Herieth F. pmc-11438207.description: BackgroundEpilepsy remains a significant public health concern in Tanzania, with affected individuals enduring stigma, whether through actions or perceptions. Myths, misunderstandings, and misconceptions about epilepsy have persisted due to a multitude of factors. Here, we assessed attitudes and perceptions toward epilepsy in Mahenge.

pmc-12359914.title: Global, regional, and national epidemiology of type 1 diabetes in children from 1990 to 2021: trend and health inequality analyses based on the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021
pmc-12359914.creator: Jing Xie, Weilan Li, Xiaomin Li, Xueli Zhang, Jing Liu, Zeye Liu, Shenqi Jing, Hua Shao
pmc-12359914.description: BackgroundType 1 diabetes (T1D) is a significant health challenge for children. Assessing the epidemiological patterns and health inequalities associated with T1D at the global, regional, and national levels, along with future projections, is essential for informing equitable public health policies.

pmc-13062321.title: 3D-Assisted Scapular Fracture Fixation in a Polytraumatized Patient: A Case Report
pmc-13062321.creator: Jordan Dobrich, Michael K Deegan, Caleb D Gerber, Kyong S Min
pmc-13062321.description: Introduction:Scapular fractures are relatively uncommon but pose significant challenges in high-energy polytrauma, particularly when complex comminuted patterns are present. Three-dimensional (3D) computed tomography (CT) reconstruction and 3D printing are emerging tools in orthopedics that enhance pre-operative planning and intraoperative decision-making. Although widely used in pelvic, acetabular, and distal radius fractures, their application in scapular fracture management remains limited.

pmc-13279002.title: Real-world investigation of platelet apoptosis for mechanistic insights into severe immune thrombocytopenia and bleeding
pmc-13279002.creator: Tarun Tyagi, Kanika Jain, Martin Matthews, Stephanie Halene, John Hwa, Natalia Neparidze
pmc-13279002.description: BackgroundGiven the low platelet counts in patients with immune thrombocytopenia (< 100 × 109/L) and its pathophysiological complexity, it remains both a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge. Routine platelet function tests could not be performed due to the extremely low counts in a patient with gastrointestinal bleeding.

pmc-13521165.title: Double-stranded DNA donors and CRISPR-Cas9 for universal correction of mutations causing cystic fibrosis in human airway cells
pmc-13521165.creator: Vrishti Sinha, Paul G Ayoub, Colin J Juett, Lindsay E Lathrop, Ruth A Foley, Ruby A Sims, Joseph D Long, Emily C Duggan, Neil R Fernandes, Beate Illek, Brigitte N Gomperts, Steven J Jonas, Donald B Kohn
pmc-13521165.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a devastating genetic disease caused by mutations in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene. As morbidity and mortality from CF results from a lack of mucus clearance that leads to chronic bacterial infections and progressive loss of lung function, site-specific insertion of a CFTR cDNA into the endogenous CFTR locus in airway basal stem cells (ABSCs) could prove curative for all disease-causing mutations.

pmc-13616694.title: Serum ferritin as an independent biomarker of subclinical synovitis in rheumatoid arthritis patients in clinical remission or low disease activity
pmc-13616694.creator: Duygu Kurtulus, Adem Kucuk
pmc-13616694.description: BackgroundResidual synovial inflammation may persist in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) despite clinical remission or low disease activity. Conventional inflammatory markers such as C-reactive protein (CRP) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) may not adequately reflect subclinical synovitis detected by musculoskeletal ultrasound. Ferritin, an acute-phase reactant involved in inflammatory signaling, may represent a complementary biomarker of ongoing synovial inflammation.
